title: InMotion Cloud Debuts Fixed-Price Managed Cloud via @sejournal, @inmotionhosting
content:
VIRGINIA BEACH, VA – September 8, 2026 – Backed by over 25 years of infrastructure experience, the platform combines flat monthly pricing with a fixed egress allowance.
Hyperscaler pricing has a bad habit of defying predictability. Organizations running production workloads on AWS, Azure, or GCP are often familiar with reviewing monthly bills for unexpected egress charges or storage increases, while navigating automated support queues.
AI workloads and GPU training have only amplified these billing swings for engineering teams. That’s the friction InMotion Cloud is looking to solve with its new Managed Private Cloud platform. Built on OpenStack and running entirely on bare-metal hardware InMotion owns and operates, the platform replaces variable meters with flat monthly rates and a fixed egress allowance built into every plan.
Since InMotion Cloud owns its infrastructure, the company keeps direct control over service quality and pricing. Single-vendor ownership also means one team holds complete responsibility and is backed by a team of senior engineers available to quickly deploy, optimize, and troubleshoot your architecture as a tangible extension of your IT team.
“We’ve spent 25 years watching customers transition from shared hosting to dedicated servers, only to run into massive cost spikes and operational friction when moving to hyperscalers,” Dan Cunningham, Chief Revenue Officer, InMotion Hosting.
Running on OpenStack pairs that ownership with virtual machine scaling. InMotion handles hardware provisioning, hypervisor patching, network configuration, and monitoring, so customers reach U.S.-based engineers on first contact instead of a ticket queue.
If standard managed cloud deployments don’t fit your requirements, InMotion Cloud offers Virtual Private Data Centers, which provide custom hardware configurations, fully isolated network topologies, and dedicated resource pools. This offering is for enterprises and organizations with complex compliance or architectural demands.
InMotion Cloud goes further than a fixed pricing model. With Flex Spend Advantage, teams plan around a committed monthly spend rather than surprise line-item overages. They can rebalance resources as workloads change without rewriting their budget model, with usage visibility and guidance from InMotion Cloud engineers.
The platform is purpose-built for AI-forward builders, SaaS platforms, digital agencies, and MSPs seeking predictable infrastructure costs to protect their margins. For organizations transitioning from public cloud or legacy on-prem setups, white-glove support is included across all implementations.
To evaluate a move, teams can use InMotion Cloud’s Cost Comparison Calculator to compare their AWS, GCP, or Azure spend with InMotion Cloud rates ahead of migration.

title: Halloween hashtags to kickoff #spookyseason
content:
The air is getting crisp, pumpkin spice-flavored treats are returning to store shelves and scary movies are back in rotation. Autumn is a fan favorite, and the season’s star holiday, Halloween, is growing in popularity amongst all ages. In the US alone, 73% of people participate in the holiday in some way. For brands, Halloween is a great chance to get in on the spooky fun with creative themed content.
The key to scaring up successful seasonal content: Halloween posts live or die by discoverability, not just cute captions.
Hashtags are only one piece of the formula. They don’t work quite the same as they used to; hashtagging is no longer a content reach shortcut, but instead a useful content signal. Social media algorithms use hashtags to categorize and distribute your content to the right audiences.
Keep reading (if you dare) to uncover trending Halloween hashtags and content ideas to put in your arsenal.
If you need a quick list to start, these 10 hashtags have good popularity and cover a variety of topics. Depending on your brand and audience, you can use these to focus on a range of products, services, ideas and themes.
Most of us enjoy a mix of candy in our Trick-or-Treat bags, and algorithms appreciate variety in your content tagging, too. To get the most traction, go for a selection of Halloween-centric hashtags that span broad discussions, niche topics and branded hashtags where appropriate.
For example, #horror and #HorrorMovies are major hashtags that pop up around movies, TV shows and seasonal attractions this time of year. Depending on your brand’s offerings, you could use this hashtag alongside niche ones like #HorrorManga, #HorrorFiction or #HorrorBooks to target more specific audience segments.
If your brand ties directly to the horror entertainment scene, you could also create a branded hashtag to match, like streaming platform Shudder did with their #ShudderSundays tag. You can even jump on a hashtag holiday like #NationalHorrorMovieDay on October 23rd. Burger chain A&W got in on the fun with horror movie posters featuring their menu items and mascots.
Social media lives on culture, so try to capitalize on Halloween pop culture trends when selecting your hashtag line up. It’s what your audience expects, with 93% of consumers thinking it’s important for brands to keep up with online culture. This includes new horror movies, classic Halloween characters (like #MichaelMyers or #FreddyKrueger) and trending shows or memes that speak to your audience’s interests.
Once you’ve curated your selection of hashtags for the season, make sure to follow best practices for adding them in. This can vary by network. On Instagram and TikTok, the algorithm currently favors hashtags within captions versus the first comment. Place a few strategic hashtags at the end of your caption. On Facebook, you can work hashtags directly into sentences in the post itself. Hashtags don’t provide discoverability value in your social media bios, but placing branded hashtags here can let your audience know they exist.
There are so many ways to get in on spooky celebrations via hashtags, from food to decor to scene-setting aesthetics. We’ve put together ideas across categories to give you a bank to pull from no matter how your brand plans to participate.
In addition to the all-purpose hashtags listed above, you can riff on them to tap into more specific Halloween conversations. You can also choose hashtags for specific concepts like ghosts and goblins. There are additional days of significance around Halloween, both modern and traditional, that also have hashtags you can apply if they’re a fit for your brand.
Adults and kids alike love dressing up for Halloween. Costume and makeup videos are hugely popular this time of year, showcasing creative transformations from cute to scary.
Australian beauty brand MCoBeauty has partnered with influencers to use their products in unique makeup looks for Halloween. Niche hashtags like the ones used here (#SkullMakeup, #SpiderMakeup) are great for catching audiences looking for specific ideas.
Pumpkin spice reigns supreme this time of year in everything from Starbucks’ infamous latte to cottage cheese from Good Culture. If your brand is in the food space and can tap into the enduring pumpkin spice trend, you can create hashtags for your specific items. Pumpkins themselves also appear on store shelves for Halloween as food and decor.
Cool temperatures in the fall are perfect for baking, and social media users share their creations with hashtags across networks. Cozy drinks are another popular topic (in addition to those pumpkin spice lattes!):
Seasonal shifts in home decor are perfect for bringing the spirit of Halloween into your everyday space. Whether decorating for a party or turning your yard into an eerie setting for trick-or-treaters, users are actively looking for home decor retail offerings and DIY ideas. Hashtags for your brand to use include:
UK home decor brand Rockett St George often shares seasonal tablescapes and interior design ideas featuring pumpkins, skulls and bats with links in their social media bios to directly shop the pieces featured in posts.
To connect with audiences looking to create decor on a budget, browse hashtags like:
For some, Halloween vibes are year round. Spooky aesthetics are a part of many subcultures, and Halloween mega-fans are always preparing for the next year. Themes like these see a surge in interest as Halloween approaches, though they have traction any month:
Depending on the year, specific movies, books and TV shows may drive additional interest in these spaces.
TikTok has a slew of hashtags around specific audiences:
Use these to connect with niche groups who already know your brand or would enjoy your seasonal offerings.
Restaurants, small businesses and locally-focused brands may get lost in mega-hashtags like #Halloween and miss out on connecting with the customers who will actually come in the door. If you’re a smaller brand, try hyper-local options your city or state commerce chambers have established:
In addition, your brand can work in a few business boosting hashtags, especially if you have online purchasing options.
Halloween is fun for the entire family, furry members included! Pet brands can tap hashtags like:
Use these to share pet treats, costumes and other fun ways to get four-footed family members in the spooky spirit.
Hashtags can capture the entire family experience as well. Options:
Sprout Listening data from January 2026 through the date of publication reveals that “niche” and #[word]maxxing have emerged as leading keywords and hashtags across social networks throughout 2026. On TikTok, #Fallmaxxing is an early contender for a seasonal take on the trend. Brands have an opportunity get ahead of the curve and build on this trend with additional tags like #Autumnmaxxing. Consider working these in to your content this Halloween—your brand might just be the one to make “#Halloweenmaxxing” a thing this year.
Depending on your social media mix (and which you’re prioritizing for the Halloween season), your hashtag approach will differ by network. Here’s what to know to increase visibility and connect with the right audiences on key networks for the season.
Hashtags remain a key part of reach on Meta’s networks. According to the official @creators account, Instagram hashtags are best placed in the caption, targeting 3-5 hashtags per post. Hashtags on Instagram Reels help ensure your video content is served to audiences ready to engage.
For Facebook hashtags , you can include them in the sentences of your post or at the end of your content. Facebook hashtags work best when kept to 2-5 per post. Anything more comes across as spam.
Some Instagram and Facebook hashtags to consider for Halloween:
Your approach to TikTok hashtags should position them as keywords specific to each post. TikTok “listens” to your videos, and wants to see hashtags that match the words spoken in your content. Focusing on niche topics is the secret to getting traction with high-intent users instead of those who will just scroll by.
Lots of communities use specific hashtags on this network to connect with each other. When done respectfully and with intention, your brand can participate in conversations with these groups.
X (formerly known as Twitter) recommends brands use hashtags a bit differently than other networks. In general, X/Twitter hashtags should be used sparingly, and the network says to avoid using them in organic post copy . If you do choose to use them, stick with just 1-2 and be sure they’re purposeful and relevant to what you’re sharing. Make sure you review trending topics on X before moving ahead with your chosen hashtags.
Some Halloween ideas to get you started (but check X for the most up to date ideas):
Title and description keywords take a greater priority than hashtags on Pinterest, though the latter can still help categorize content in search. If you’re trying to reach a specific audience, hashtags can be helpful. Pinterest hashtags only work in the description of the pin, not comments. Generic hashtags aren’t helpful here, so aim for 3-5 specific tags on your pins.
Here are some Halloween hashtag ideas for Pinterest that you could also use as keywords:

Having tools like Sprout Listening enable you to discover and monitor hashtags that Halloween fans are using. You can track specific hashtags instantly with Queries, sifting through hundreds of thousands of conversations without manually searching. Sprout Listening helps you hone in on the right Halloween hashtags for your brand and uncover new ones bubbling up in the cauldron before your competitors do.
According to Sprout’s Q4 2025 Pulse Survey, 44% of social users say they are more likely to buy from brands that launch their fall (Halloween) and winter (holiday/Christmas) marketing early. #CodeOrange appears on social earlier each year as stores roll out their Halloween goods, so audiences are ready to hear from your brand well before the calendar turns to October. Start trickling in your Halloween content early and focus on incorporating hashtags that best match your brand, content and audience.
